title: The Eroded Childhood Canyon

features.name: path-cut-deep
features.desc-on-touch: The canyon carved by small feet walking the same route again and again, year after year. The path became a groove, the groove became a ravine, the ravine became a memory of what it was before it became itself.

features.name: canyon-threshold
features.desc-on-touch: Where the path stopped being a path and became a canyon. The threshold between what you walked into and what walks through you now.

features.name: childhood-marker
features.desc-on-touch: Initials carved by a child who was learning what it meant to leave a mark. The stone remembers the knife. The canyon remembers the footsteps that proved the mark was real.

features.name: erosion-layers
features.desc-on-touch: Rock and dust arranged in strata, each layer a season, each season a dozen walks, each walk a repetition of the one before it. You are reading the sediment-record of one person's childhood learning it was also a geography.

features.name: echo-of-old-footsteps
features.desc-on-touch: A wireframe trace of the original path, still visible beneath the canyon that replaced it. The archive keeps both versions: the path it was and the chasm it became.

features.name: destination-forgotten
features.desc-on-touch: A pool of runoff from years of rain in the canyon-bottom. Nobody remembers what lay at the end of the original path. The canyon is now its own destination.

inscription: small feet make deep canyons when they follow each other long enough

file.name: Childhood_Location_1985_Photograph.jpg
file.note: A Polaroid of a child at what looks like a shallow ditch. Dated 1985. A photo of the same place from 2008 shows a canyon ten feet deep. Both images date-stamped as 2015.

reverie.title: REVERIE — retracing what was walked
narr: You both walk the place as it was, before erosion
made it strange. She remembers coming here daily.
You count her footsteps aloud — one, two, three,
forty, four hundred, four thousand. Somewhere
between repetitions the path learned to canyon.
By the time you both arrive, it has been canyoning for years.

exits.label: back up the slope toward the path-that-came-before
deeper into the canyon where erosion teaches you about time
toward where other canyons remember other childhoods
